## The strait is not trading the strait

Crude fell back under $100 this morning after Trump said he is open to talking to Iran. In the same
news cycle a projectile hit a tanker entering the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's foreign ministry said it
is prepared for a prolonged war, and the Treasury Secretary named **23 September** as the date
Iranian airlines get shut down. The price moved on the first of those and none of the other three.

That is the whole read, and it is the same gap the desk has been watching for seven months. **Brent
is at $100.54 and Hormuz transits are at 4.3 a day against a pre-war 78.3.** The market is pricing
an announcement; the waterway is unchanged. A ceasefire was recorded on 18 September and the transits
did not move — so we already have the natural experiment, and it says the premium comes out on words
long before hulls come back.

**What would have to be true for the fall to be real.** Somebody has to hold the instrument that
reopens the strait, and Washington does not. The Hormuz clause sits in the US–Iran MoU and routes
through Oman: Tehran's own plan — management and mandatory tolls — was opposed by Oman and amended by
Saudi Arabia, and the meeting to present it was postponed on 14 September. Until that meeting
happens, "open to talking" is a sentence, not a lever. **Watch the Oman meeting, not the ceasefire.**

**The 23rd is the thing to diarise.** It is the only dated, unilateral action in today's board, and
it is an escalation announced one week after a ceasefire. Two dated moves pointing opposite ways
inside ten days is not incoherence — it is a negotiation being conducted in public with instruments
rather than statements.

**What our own sources are saying, and where they are wrong.** The loudest reads on the board remain
collapse calls: Houthi disintegration, Iranian capitulation, an imminent American ground commitment.
Three separate analysts in our ledgers have now called that ground commitment — March, July and last
night — and all three are open and failing. The desk's position is unchanged and is the boring one:
the strait stays constrained while the shooting pauses, because mines, war-risk cover and owners who
will not sail are not repaired by a press conference.

**The call.** Brent settles below $90 before 2026-10-21 only if PortWatch transits recover above
40/day first. **Breaker:** transits above 40/day for five consecutive sessions while Brent holds
above $100 — that would mean the price is tracking something other than the strait, and this read is
wrong.
